title: Saffire-II: a plain-language summary
summary: Nine fire tests were organized, material behavior was compared, and a pilot model was built to estimate a local CO2 sensor change three minutes after ignition.

reading_guide.published: An outcome already reported in the supplied NASA documentation.
reading_guide.calculated: Derived in this study by processing the readings.
reading_guide.insight: An interpretation supported by the results.
reading_guide.predicted: A model estimate compared with an observation to measure error.
reading_guide.null: Unavailable or not applicable; never interpret null as zero.

scope.setting: Inside an uncrewed Cygnus spacecraft in microgravity.
scope.note: The nine tests share a flight and cabin; they are not nine independent flight replicates. Local raw data do not cover all six Saffire missions.

measurements.label: Materials and flame behavior
measurements.origin: Published outcomes supplied with the dataset
measurements.result: Four silicone specimens showed no sustained spread; flames spread over both SIBAL fabrics; Nomex did not ignite in the composite; both PMMA slabs sustained anchored flames.
measurements.why_it_matters: Supports material comparisons under the tested conditions.

measurements.label: Airflow, oxygen and pressure
measurements.result: Airflow ranged from 19.98 to 24.99 cm/s; oxygen readings from 21.52 to 21.80%; pressure from 102.50 to 102.76 kPa.
measurements.why_it_matters: Defines the experimental conditions; behavior in another atmosphere requires additional evidence.

measurements.label: CO2 change after three minutes
measurements.result: Signed changes ranged from -16.61 to 107.00 ppm.
measurements.why_it_matters: Provides a common response for comparing all nine tests and training the pilot model.

measurements.label: Flame spread rate
measurements.origin: Two published values; no new optical front tracking
measurements.result: The SIBAL rates are 2.1 and 2.6 mm/s.
measurements.why_it_matters: Quantifies flame advance where a rate is available; two cases cannot establish a general law.

measurements.label: Local plume temperature and radiation
measurements.origin: Calculations from local sensors during the first three minutes
measurements.result: Per-test sampled plume peaks range from 22.62 to 85.85 degrees C; relative radiation peaks range from 0.051 to 0.562 kW/m2.
measurements.why_it_matters: Shows thermal signals at instrumented locations; geometry limits their interpretation as flame temperature or total fire power.

measurements.label: Cabin and smoke signals
measurements.result: Sensor signals exist, but per-fire alarm events and clock synchronization were not verified.
measurements.why_it_matters: Provides information for future detection analysis; alarm delays remain unavailable.

measurements.label: Ignition timing and images
measurements.result: Pulses last about 9.2 or 30 s; 27 images were sampled, three per test. The ignitor energy scale requires review.
measurements.why_it_matters: Supports event timing and visual inspection. Image sampling did not produce new spread-rate measurements.

co2_calculation.rule: Subtract the pre-ignition typical reading from the typical reading at 150-180 seconds. Each is a median of one-second medians over a 30-second window.
co2_calculation.unit: ppm: parts per million, a way to express concentration.

real_example.plain_explanation: The sensor rose from approximately 3350 to 3390 ppm: a change of 40 ppm.

co2_calculation.negative_values: A reading below its initial level can reflect variation or air mixing. It does not demonstrate that the fire consumed CO2.
co2_calculation.interpretation_limit: This response is not total emitted gas mass, total fire power or a crew exposure threshold.

insights.title: Silicone did not sustain flame spread in these tests
insights.evidence: This occurred in all four silicone specimens.
insights.meaning: The observed behavior was limited under this combination of airflow, oxygen, pressure and specimen geometry.
insights.why_it_matters: Provides evidence for material comparisons; it does not certify all silicone configurations as safe.

insights.title: Flames spread over both SIBAL fabrics
insights.evidence: Published rates were 2.1 mm/s at roughly 20 cm/s airflow and 2.6 mm/s at roughly 25 cm/s.
insights.meaning: The second rate was 23.8% higher. This is a comparison of two tests, not a universal airflow law.
insights.why_it_matters: Identifies a relationship worth testing with more ventilation and propagation experiments.

insights.title: A flame can advance slowly while burning persists for minutes
insights.evidence: The PMMA slabs have published burn durations of 10 and 15 minutes, with flames near the leading edge.
insights.meaning: Limited advance and extinguishment are different outcomes.
insights.why_it_matters: Fire-safety analysis must also consider how long burning persists.

insights.title: The composite's PMMA burned, but Nomex did not ignite
insights.evidence: Only one specimen used this combination.
insights.meaning: The fire did not transfer from the PMMA section to the Nomex section in that test.
insights.why_it_matters: Provides a material comparison case that needs replication under other conditions.

insights.title: Each test needs its own CO2 baseline
insights.evidence: Pre-test readings ranged from approximately 3307 to 4334 ppm.
insights.meaning: The tests started at different CO2 levels, so each response subtracts its own initial reading.
insights.why_it_matters: Avoids attributing CO2 already present to the current test.

insights.title: The model improved one specific prediction in a small pilot
insights.evidence: Its mean absolute held-out error was 17.83 ppm.
insights.meaning: It estimates the three-minute sensor change within this pilot; another flight is needed for external validation.
insights.why_it_matters: Provides a first tool for comparing predicted and observed responses.

insights.title: The data are closer to the assumed ISS and Gateway scenarios
insights.evidence: The tests used near-terrestrial pressure, airlike oxygen and microgravity.
insights.meaning: They more closely match those reference scenarios used in the relevance comparison.
insights.why_it_matters: Helps prioritize which evidence to consult for a given environment.

insights.title: Transfer to lunar, Mars and rover environments remains unvalidated
insights.evidence: The local archive has no enriched-oxygen, low-pressure or lunar/Martian partial-gravity tests.
insights.meaning: Comparisons with those habitats are indicative and use analyst design assumptions.
insights.why_it_matters: Identifies additional experiments needed before extrapolating.

insights.title: Smoke signals alone cannot establish alarm timing
insights.evidence: Alarm events, thresholds and verified clock synchronization are missing.
insights.meaning: A reliable detection delay is unavailable for each test.
insights.why_it_matters: Identifies the information needed to evaluate detection equipment.

predictive_model.target_description: Change in the local CO2 sensor three minutes after the electrical ignition marker.
predictive_model.why_this_target: Available for all nine tests and comparable at a common time horizon.
predictive_model.what_was_fitted: Two typical responses: one for silicone and another for the other materials, with the latter adjusted for airflow.
predictive_model.evaluation: Train on eight tests, predict the ninth, and repeat for all nine. All 15 candidate models used this same evaluation.
predictive_model.baseline_description: Always predict the mean response of the eight training tests.

mean_absolute_error.meaning: Average absolute distance between predicted and observed CO2 change; about 18 ppm for the selected model.

rmse.meaning: Error measure that gives larger mistakes more weight. Lower is better.

maximum_absolute_error.meaning: Largest absolute held-out error observed in these nine tests; not a bound for future experiments.

predictive_model.improvement_meaning: RMSE decreased relative to the baseline. This percentage is not a percentage of correct predictions or of safety.

worst_case.meaning: The model misses much of the only PMMA-Nomex specimen's response; material-specific differences remain.

predictive_model.formula_optional: CO2 change = -2.372 ppm for silicone; 55.612 * (20 / airflow in cm/s) for the other observed materials.
limitations: Only nine tests from one flight; no validation on another flight.
Repeated selection used the same evaluation, so the selected error is optimistic.
The inverse-airflow exponent was fixed for this candidate, not learned as a universal physical law.
Only II-6 has the higher airflow and only II-7 uses PMMA-Nomex; their held-out folds lack matching cases.
The model does not directly estimate flame spread, fire size, alarm delay or crew risk.

habitat_relevance.iss_and_gateway: Greater similarity to the assumed atmosphere and microgravity reference scenarios.
habitat_relevance.lunar_mars_rover: Additional enriched-oxygen, low-pressure and partial-gravity evidence is needed.
habitat_relevance.ranking_meaning: Ranks the usefulness of evidence under design assumptions, not material danger or ignition probability.
habitat_relevance.assumptions: Habitat atmospheres are analyst scenarios, not official mission requirements.

unavailable_results.label: Total fire power, or HRR
unavailable_results.reason: Missing validated inlet/outlet oxygen with mass flow, or a validated cabin mass balance.

unavailable_results.label: Time until smoke alarm
unavailable_results.reason: Missing alarm events, thresholds and synchronized clocks.

unavailable_results.label: Safe crew exposure time
unavailable_results.reason: Applicable exposure channels and limits were not established.

unavailable_results.label: Effect of stopping ventilation
unavailable_results.reason: No documented controlled flow-cutoff and extinction intervention.

unavailable_results.label: Ignitor energy
unavailable_results.reason: The archived voltage/current product conflicts with nominal power and duration; units, scaling and channel interpretation require review.
unavailable_results.model_use: The calculated energy was not used to train the model.

source.citation: Urban DL, Ruff G. "Spacecraft Fire Experiment-II(SAFFIRE-II)", NASA PSI Data Repository, Version 5
source.attribution: NASA supplied measurements and published outcomes. Extraction, the CO2 response, modeling and interpretations were produced in this study.

charts.title: Observed CO2 response and model error
charts.description: Left: signed CO2 changes for the nine tests. Right: baseline and selected-model RMSE; lower is better.
charts.interpretation_note: CO2 change is not a hazard score. Error reduction is not an accuracy or safety percentage.

charts.title: CO2 comparison windows
charts.description: Each panel shows baseline-subtracted CO2 over time. Gray marks the pre-ignition window; orange marks 150-180 seconds.
charts.interpretation_note: The shaded regions define the calculation windows, not exposure limits.

charts.title: Published SIBAL spread rates
charts.description: Two published flame spread rates plotted against measured pre-ignition airflow.
charts.interpretation_note: Two observations do not establish a causal or universal airflow law.

charts.title: Temperature sensor coverage
charts.description: Maximum sampled plume-thermocouple readings and duct inlet temperature for each test.
charts.interpretation_note: Different sensor positions and coverage prevent interpreting these as maximum flame or average cabin temperatures.

charts.title: Sampled camera frames
charts.description: Three camera frames per test, selected near 30, 90 and 150 seconds after the electrical marker.
charts.interpretation_note: Visual quality control only; no independently calibrated flame-front measurement.
